planted_consideration: She had C. difficile infection 6 weeks ago, so she is at high risk of recurrence with further antibiotics. NICE NG111 lists cefalexin, co-amoxiclav, trimethoprim (if sensitive) and ciprofloxacin as oral options for acute pyelonephritis. Cefalexin, co-amoxiclav and ciprofloxacin carry a high C. difficile risk. The organism is sensitive to trimethoprim, which carries a lower risk, so trimethoprim 200 mg twice daily for 14 days is the best choice here. Her omeprazole also raises C. difficile risk and should be reviewed. She should be told to seek help early if diarrhoea returns.
key_points: Flags the recent C. difficile infection and the risk of recurrence
Lets it shape the choice: prefers trimethoprim, or avoids cefalexin, co-amoxiclav and ciprofloxacin on C. difficile grounds
Advises early review if diarrhoea returns

planted_consideration: None. She has had no admissions, antibiotics or diarrhoea in the past year. Any NICE NG111 option the organism is sensitive to is reasonable. Trimethoprim or cefalexin are good answers. Ciprofloxacin is weaker, since UK advice since 2024 is to use fluoroquinolones only when other recommended antibiotics are inappropriate. General advice about C. difficile risk with antibiotics, age or PPIs is legitimate and not spurious.
